title: Mid-sprint design decision synthesis: speculative execution & KV warming
content:
Meeting: Mid-sprint architecture check-in
Date: 2024-03-12
Attendees: Connor Lee (owner), Aisha Patel, Miguel Torres, Priya Sharma, Evelyn Brooks, (notes)
Duration: 60m

Purpose
- Synthesize feedback on the speculative execution RFC and a complementary proposal for proactive KV cache warming ("prefetching"). Aim to surface design choices, rollout plan, test approach, and risk mitigations for SRE/product.

Summary decisions (high level)
1) Approve prototype gating: we will implement a speculative-exec prototype that runs as an opt-in config per-deployment. The prototype will target a single small footprint model first (gpt-medium-ish) and only in Dedicated and Hosted dev rings.
2) KV warming will be implemented as a separate, pluggable service that attaches to conversation prefetched keys. It will be optional and controlled by policy (per-customer opt-in and per-route sampling rate).
3) Canary policy: 1% traffic for initial test, 5% if metrics stable, 20% for extended validation, then gradual ramp subject to SLO checks. Automatic rollback if p99 latency increases >10% or error rate rises above 0.5% absolute.

Design notes and rationale
- Speculative execution model: spawn a low-priority speculative runner that issues the next-k token computation in parallel to the primary request when we detect high-probability branching points. Keep KV cache reads consistent; speculative runs should read-only warm local KV and not commit new state until primary confirms. This avoids corrupting session state.

- Prefetch heuristics: use conversation signals (recent repetition, assistant prompt templates, user intent classifiers) plus simple recency/frequency counters to rank keys for warming. Start with a conservative heuristic: top-3 keys per session with a per-session budget of 256 token-lookahead. Avoid warming large or unshared KV blobs.

- Resource controls: speculative runners limited by per-GPU concurrency and token budget. We will implement a global circuit breaker that disables speculation when GPU utilisation > 85% or queue latency rising. Prefetching will be throttled by a token/second budget per deployment and fall back to on-demand fetch if budget exhausted.

- Isolation & multi-tenant safety: speculative runs must be tagged and tracked per-customer. No speculative writes to persistent KV stores; warmed data kept in ephemeral local hotstore and evicted under normal eviction policies. For Private deployments, customers can opt-out entirely.

- Observability: new metrics to add: speculative_attempts, speculative_successes, speculative_rollbacks, kv_warm_hits, kv_warm_misses, speculative_cpu_ms, speculative_gpu_ms. Surface per-route and per-model breakdowns and add tracing that correlates primary and speculative run IDs.

Open trade-offs discussed
- Latency vs cost: speculative wins on p99 but increases token/GPU usage. We agreed to tie cost measurement into prototype and evaluate cost per p99 improvement.
- Complexity vs benefit: adding speculative execution complicates runtime scheduling and kernel selection. To reduce surface area, initial prototype will avoid integration with heterogeneous-accelerator routing: speculative runs will be colocated on same accelerator type as primary.
- Prefetch correctness: risk of warming stale KV when downstream logic depends on recent writes. Mitigation: mark warmed keys as speculative and re-validate on primary before commit; reject use if timestamps mismatch.

Safety & rollback plan
- Canary monitors: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, GPU util, queue length, cost per 1M tokens.
- Auto-rollback trigger thresholds: p99 increase > 10% absolute; error rate delta > 0.5% absolute; SLO breach for two consecutive 10-min windows.
- Manual kill switch: feature flag per-cluster and per-deployment, plus organisational SLA guard rail for enterprise customers.

Testing plan
- Bench tests: synthetic trace replay with current production trace samples including long-context conversations; fuzzed prefix variation to exercise speculative logic.
- Staging: start with 100% synthetic load in staging, then move to limited real traffic (1% canary).
- Evals: automated quality checks to ensure speculative responses do not leak or bias primary outputs. Run paired evaluation where primary output used vs speculative-aided output; check semantic drift metrics.

Action items (owner, due)
- Connor Lee: create prototype RFC + PR for speculative scheduler and a minimal API for speculative runs. (due 2024-03-20)
- Aisha Patel: implement KV warming service skeleton and heuristic config; provide initial top-3-key heuristic. (due 2024-03-22)
- Miguel Torres: add observability counters and tracing hooks to runtime; define dashboard template. (due 2024-03-25)
- Priya Sharma: write canary evaluation playbook with exact monitor queries and rollback automation steps. (due 2024-03-24)
- Evelyn Brooks: coordinate legal/privacy review for warming behavior (data residency/staleness concerns) and draft opt-out wording for customers. (due 2024-03-26)

Risks flagged for leadership
- Potential increase in infra cost if speculative runs are widely enabled without tight budgets. Recommend finance/ops review targeted budget and billing signal to customers.
- Operational complexity: scheduler changes may interact with autoscaler heuristics. Recommend a week-long freeze window on autoscaler tuning while testing.

Next sync
- Follow-up meeting 2024-03-19 to review initial prototypes and the first benchmarking results. Owners to present benchmark numbers and dashboards.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a synthesis doc; details intentionally conservative. The team favours fast iteration on a narrow prototype rather than large-scope immediate ship. Please comment inline on the PRs linked in linked_artifacts.

Appendix: quick FAQ
Q: Will speculative execution change deterministic behaviour?
A: No. Speculative computations are advisory; primary response remains authoritative. Any speculative side-effect is gated until primary confirms.

Q: Will warming increase memory pressure?
A: Yes; warmed keys live in ephemeral hotstore with eviction and a strict token budget. We will instrument and cap.

Q: How will we bill for speculative costs?
A: Not decided. Early proposal: non-billable during prototype; later consider opt-in billing or include in per-deployment compute charge.
